about: What holds each thing a player can choose, and each section of config. tests/verification.map.test.ts fails when something that exists is missing here, when a check named here does not exist, and when an entry names no check and gives no reason.

An entry says: "unit", unit test files by name (gameplay is tests/gameplay.test.ts); "trace", runs of the trace by the name it prints (scripts/trace.mjs); "e2e", a drill run of the end-to-end run (serve_OH_call2) or one of its phases (drills, keys, touch, probes, soak, perf, screenshots); "skill", verify-court-feel feature files, which are recipes run by hand and not checks; "manual", what no check holds and what a person looks for; "note", anything a reader should know about the checks named.
Name a check when it would notice the thing going wrong, not when it only passes it by. An entry can name checks and still say "manual": the checks hold part of it.

For a drill, the checks named are the ones that play it: their names say so. For a drill played as a position, a trace run is named only beside a count: how often the player's own athlete touches the ball in it, read from a recording. A run in which it never does is no check of the pair by itself (the Mini Rally as an opposite has such a run, and says "manual"). The unit tests named for a pair play the drill's own half, in most of them with the player standing still.

For a section of config, the first fill was measured on main at 298c73e (2026-11-26): the unit tests named went red when every number of the section moved by 20%, and the trace run named is the first one the comparison showed to differ when they moved by 2%. More runs may differ: the comparison explains only the first.

For a setting, "unit" is a test of what the setting switches. That its stored value is valid is tests/settings.test.ts for every setting, and is not repeated. A trace run whose note says "Measured" is the first run the comparison showed to differ when the setting's default was changed: that run would notice the setting going wrong at the value every run plays, and says nothing of its other values.
When you add a drill, a serve, a lesson, a setting, a graphics level, a venue or a section of config, add its entry here in the same pull request. "manual" with a true reason is a correct entry.

bodies.manual: A custom body in a drill: no run of the trace or of the end-to-end run plays with one. A person sets a height and a jump in the Athlete sheet and sees the athlete and its reach change.
bodies.note: The unit test holds what a custom body does: the jump, the reach, the spike power, and that stored values are clamped. A changed default could not be measured against the trace: a stored body replaces the default whole.

venue.note: What each venue is held by is under "venue". Measured: with its default changed ('hall' to 'seaside'), this is the first run of the trace that is drawn or shown differently (the play is the same).

hand.note: The unit test holds the left-handed player: the contact point, the toss, the plant and the wind-up mirror. Measured: with its default changed ('right' to 'left'), this is the first run of the trace to play differently.

graphics.note: The unit test holds the governor behind Auto and that a level the player fixed turns it off. What each level is held by is under "graphics". The trace played the same with the level fixed at Low: nothing it compares is drawn.
